teaching_card.title: Number Properties (Medium)
teaching_card.body: Factors divide a number evenly; multiples are what you get by multiplying it. Primes have exactly two factors. The order of operations (parentheses, exponents, multiply/divide, add/subtract) and the rules for even/odd and remainders let you reason about integers without a calculator.
key_points: GCF = product of shared prime factors; LCM = highest power of every prime.
Scientific notation: coefficient from 1 to 10, times a power of 10.
Fraction ↔ decimal ↔ percent: divide, then move the decimal two places.

screens.title: Factors, multiples, and primes
screens.body: Prime-factor a number first: 60 = 2²·3·5. The greatest common factor of two numbers takes the smaller power of each shared prime; the least common multiple takes the larger power of every prime that appears. A number with prime factorization p^a·q^b has (a + 1)(b + 1) factors.

screens.title: Integers and order of operations
screens.body: Even ± even = even, odd ± odd = even, even ± odd = odd; a product is odd only when every factor is odd. Among any k consecutive integers one is a multiple of k. Evaluate expressions with PEMDAS, and remember (−3)² = 9 while −3² = −9.
key_points: Products are odd only if all factors are odd.
Consecutive integers always include a multiple of k.
Square the sign too when it is inside parentheses.

screens.title: Scientific notation and conversions
screens.body: Write a number as c × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ c < 10: moving the decimal left raises n, moving it right lowers n. Multiply coefficients and add exponents; divide coefficients and subtract exponents, then re-normalize. To convert a fraction, divide; to get a percent, multiply the decimal by 100.

screens.title: Try the moves
screens.body: (3 × 10⁴)(4 × 10⁵) = 12 × 10⁹ = 1.2 × 10¹⁰. The remainder of 7n ÷ 5 when n leaves remainder 3: 7·3 = 21 → remainder 1. And 2 + 3 × 4² = 2 + 48 = 50.
